intended_object: The cokernel projection π_f : Y → coker f, viewed as a natural transformation from the target functor `Arrow C ⥤ C` (f ↦ Y) to the cokernel functor (f ↦ coker f). This is inferred from the docstring and from the companion definitions `coker` and `ker.ι`.
explanation: At each arrow f the component is `cokernel.π f.hom : f.right ⟶ cokernel f.hom`. `Arrow.rightFunc` sends f to f.right, and `coker` sends f to `cokernel f.hom`. On a morphism u, `coker` acts by `cokernel.desc _ (u.right ≫ cokernel.π _)`, so naturality is exactly the defining equation `cokernel.π ≫ cokernel.desc _ h _ = h`. The `cat_disch` default discharges it. The setting is the natural one for a cokernel functor: a category with zero morphisms in which every morphism has a cokernel. The definition is the exact dual of `ker.ι`, which comes just before it. Mathlib has no other declaration packaging this as a natural transformation out of `Arrow.rightFunc`.
